title: Microsoft tells employees to stop tokenmaxxing, sets division-level AI budgets
excerpt: Microsoft EVP Jay Parikh told staff to curb AI token use, switched the default model to a cheaper one, and gave each division a formal AI spending cap
content_html:
TL;DR

Microsoft’s EVP told staff to curb AI token use, switched to a cheaper default model, and set division-level budgets

Microsoft executive vice president Jay Parikh has told employees in an internal email that the company needs to rein in its AI token consumption, writing that “tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for.” The message, first reported by 404 Media, reveals that Microsoft has switched its default internal AI model to a cheaper OpenAI alternative and introduced formal AI token budget targets at the division level.

As of July 2026, every Microsoft division now has an AI token spending cap. Employees can track their individual AI usage through an internal dashboard, and many engineers have been spending hundreds to a few thousand dollars a month in tokens. The shift marks a significant turn from the company’s earlier posture of encouraging widespread AI adoption across its workforce.

The move places Microsoft squarely in a pattern TNW has tracked since June, when companies including AT&T, Meta, Uber, Walmart, and Amazon began capping or throttling employee AI spending after discovering that token-priced tools behave nothing like the seat-based software licences finance teams know how to budget. Microsoft had already quietly cancelled most Claude Code licences inside its Experiences and Devices group in May, telling engineers to migrate to GitHub Copilot CLI by the end of its fiscal year.

Parikh’s email goes further. By making a cheaper model the default and creating division-level budgets, Microsoft is building the kind of metered infrastructure that treats AI tooling more like a utility bill than an enterprise software subscription. The anonymous Microsoft employee who shared the email with 404 Media described the budget caps as “the ultimate admission” that the company cannot afford to let its own staff use its AI products without limits.

Microsoft is not alone in confronting the maths. Amazon, Adobe, Atlassian, and Citi have all introduced some form of AI usage throttling or spending visibility in recent months. Per-token prices have fallen roughly 98 percent since late 2022, but enterprise AI bills have still tripled because agentic tools consume dramatically more tokens per task than the autocomplete interactions that shaped the original pricing models.

The broader financial picture at Microsoft remains strong. The company’s most recent quarterly results showed revenue, operating income, and net income all beating Wall Street expectations. But the internal cost controls suggest that even a company generating record profits sees uncapped AI token spending as a line item that can spiral faster than the productivity gains it delivers.

For employees, the message is clear: use AI, but know what it costs. That is a long way from the “AI for everyone” rhetoric of eighteen months ago, and it may be the most telling signal yet that the enterprise AI market is moving from an experimental phase into a procurement discipline where every token has a price tag and every division has a ceiling.

Published August 4, 2026 - 6:47 pm UTC

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

微软的执行副总裁告诉员工限制人工智能代币的使用，改用更便宜的默认模型，并设定部门级预算

微软执行副总裁杰伊·帕里克（Jay Parikh）在一封内部电子邮件中告诉员工，公司需要控制人工智能代币的消耗，并写道“tokenmaxxing 不是我们优化的目的。” 该消息首先由 404 Media 报道，显示微软已将其默认的内部 AI 模型切换为更便宜的 OpenAI 替代方案，并在部门级别引入了正式的 AI 代币预算目标。

截至 2026 年 7 月，微软的每个部门现在都有人工智能代币支出上限。 员工可以通过内部仪表板跟踪他们个人的人工智能使用情况，许多工程师每月花费数百到数千美元的代币。 这一转变标志着该公司先前鼓励员工广泛采用人工智能的态度发生了重大转变。

这一举措使微软完全陷入了 TNW 自 6 月份以来一直跟踪的模式，当时包括 AT&T、Meta、Uber、沃尔玛和亚马逊在内的公司在发现代币定价工具的行为与财务团队知道如何预算的基于席位的软件许可证完全不同后，开始限制或限制员工的人工智能支出。 5 月份，微软已经悄然取消了体验和设备部门内的大部分 Claude Code 许可证，并告诉工程师在本财年结束前迁移到 GitHub Copilot CLI。

帕里克的电子邮件更进一步。 通过将更便宜的模型作为默认模型并创建部门级预算，微软正在构建一种计量基础设施，将人工智能工具视为公用事业账单，而不是企业软件订阅。 与 404 Media 分享电子邮件的匿名微软员工将预算上限描述为“最终承认”该公司无法让自己的员工无限制地使用其人工智能产品。

微软并不是唯一一家面临数学问题的公司。 近几个月来，亚马逊、Adobe、Atlassian 和花旗都推出了某种形式的人工智能使用限制或支出可见性。 自 2022 年底以来，每个代币的价格已下降约 98%，但企业人工智能费用仍增加了两倍，因为代理工具每项任务消耗的代币数量远多于形成原始定价模型的自动完成交互。

微软的整体财务状况依然强劲。 该公司最近的季度业绩显示，营收、营业收入和净利润均超出华尔街预期。 但内部成本控制表明，即使是一家创造创纪录利润的公司，也将无上限的人工智能代币支出视为一项可能比其带来的生产力提升更快的螺旋式上升速度。

对于员工来说，信息很明确：使用人工智能，但要知道它的成本。 这与十八个月前的“人人享有人工智能”的言论相去甚远，这可能是迄今为止最有说服力的信号，表明企业人工智能市场正在从实验阶段转向采购纪律，每个代币都有价格标签，每个部门都有上限。
